title: Tidy Landmark Survival Analysis
text: Provides tidy framework landmark survival analysis, facilitating construction landmark-specific risk sets, incorporation longitudinal covariates, estimation associations time--event outcomes. Supports covariate estimation using last observation carried forward (LOCF) linear mixed-effects models (LME), alongside Cox proportional hazards Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Offers consistent reproducible workflow conducting analyses across multiple landmark times.

Rows never added removed, .time/.status untouched. Subjects usable measurement keep row missing value.

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: landmark_data landmark_tbl, returned landmark_data() (previous call add_landmark_covariates()). longitudinal_data data frame one row per measurement occasion (multiple rows per subject). Rows whose id appear landmark_data ignored, number reported message. id <tidy-select> subject identifier column longitudinal_data. must non-missing type id used landmark_data(); types never coerced implicitly. time <tidy-select> Numeric, finite, non-missing measurement time. must time scale origin time given landmark_data(); checked automatically. Measurements time zero (e.g. screening visits) allowed. locf, lme <tidy-select> Columns longitudinal_data derive last observation carried forward linear mixed-effects model, e.g. locf = c(treatment, stage) lme = c(bili, albumin). Either may NULL (default), . Rename inside selection name derived column, e.g. lme = c(bili_lme = bili). lme variables must continuous numeric. include_at_landmark TRUE (default), measurement taken exactly landmark (\(t = s\)) may used. FALSE, measurements strictly landmark (\(t < s\)) used. Applies methods. lookback locf . NULL (default) carries values forward without limit. single non-negative number uses measurements within window: \(s - t \le\) lookback. Older values give NA. lme_args lme . named list model options: random_slope: FALSE (default) fits random intercept; TRUE adds random slope time. adjust: NULL (default) one-sided formula fixed-effect adjustment terms, e.g. ~ age + sex. Variables come landmark_data, baseline values (covariates added earlier call). Use .t time since landmark, e.g. ~ sex * .t sex-specific slopes. REML: passed lme4::lmer(). Default TRUE. control: lme4::lmerControl() object. Default lme4::lmerControl(). min_subjects: fewest subjects measurements needed fit model (default 5). random_slope = TRUE, many subjects must least two measurements. names NULL (default) template derived column names, "{.col}" replaced source variable "{.method}" "locf" "lme", e.g. "{.col}_{.method}". Columns renamed selection keep new name. derived name already exists landmark_data error; existing columns never overwritten. progress Show progress bar fitting mixed models? Defaults tidylandmark.progress option, interactive() unset.

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: landmark \(s\), subject \(\) variable \(v\), value last non-missing measurement \(v\) time \(t \le s\) (\(t < s\) include_at_landmark = FALSE), provided within lookback. variable handled separately, visit one variable missing still contributes others. Selection depends id time, never row order. column type works, type (including factor levels) preserved. time since carried-forward measurement stored metadata auditing. subject two different non-missing values locf variable time, function errors lists affected subjects times rather choosing one arbitrarily. Exact duplicates collapsed.

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: every lme variable \(v\) landmark \(s\), independent Gaussian model fitted lme4::lmer() non-missing measurements, taken \(s\), subjects risk set \(s\): $$Y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 (t_{ij} - s) + \gamma^\top x_i + b_{0i} [+ b_{1i}(t_{ij} - s)] + \epsilon_{ij}$$ \(x_i\) optional adjust terms. Time centred landmark rescaled internally numerical stability, change predictions. derived value conditional prediction \(t = s\) including subject's random effects (predict(fit, re.form = NULL)), .e. \(\hat\beta_0 + \hat\gamma^\top x_i + \hat b_{0i}\). subject single measurement kept; prediction shrunk towards population trajectory. subject measurement landmark, missing adjust values, gets NA rather population-prediction. Different values recorded time treated replicate measurements. fit gets status: "ok"; "warning" lme4::lmer() warned (e.g. convergence) fit singular (lme4::isSingular()); "failed" subjects lme4::lmer() gave error. Failed fits give NA variable landmark without affecting fits, warning lists every fit "ok". automatic fallback random slope random intercept. Standard errors second-stage survival model treat LME-derived values known, understate uncertainty.

title: Construct landmark risk sets — landmark_data
text: landmark_data() builds outcome side landmark analysis. landmark time \(s\) keeps every subject still observation event-free \(s\). moves time origin \(s\) , optionally, administratively censors follow-fixed post-landmark horizon. result stacks landmarks one long table one row per eligible subject-landmark pair. Longitudinal covariates handled . Attach afterwards add_landmark_covariates().

title: Construct landmark risk sets — landmark_data
code: landmark_data(data, id, time, status, landmarks, horizon = NULL)

title: Construct landmark risk sets — landmark_data
text: data data frame one row per subject, holding follow-time, event status baseline predictors. id <tidy-select> subject identifier column. must unique non-missing. type preserved .id. time <tidy-select> Numeric, non-negative, finite time common origin (time zero) first event censoring. status <tidy-select> Event indicator. either: numeric: 0 censoring positive integers 1, 2, ... event types. code: subjects <- data.frame(   patient_id    = 1:10,   followup_days = c(20, 30, 48, 65, 85, 110, 145, 190, 250, 270),   event         = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 1) ) lm_dat <- landmark_data(   subjects, patient_id, followup_days, event,   landmarks = c(30, 60, 90), horizon = 180 ) tidy(lm_dat) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   landmark n_at_risk n_censored n_event_1 n_event_2 #>      <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>     <int> #> 1       30         8          3         3         2 #> 2       60         7          3         2         2 #> 3       90         5          1         3         1 tidy(lm_dat, show_proportion = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   landmark prop_at_risk n_at_risk n_censored n_event_1 n_event_2 #>      <dbl>        <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>     <int> #> 1       30          0.8         8          3         3         2 #> 2       60          0.7         7          3         2         2 #> 3       90          0.5         5          1         3         1  # With a factor status, event columns can be named after its levels subjects$event <- factor(   subjects$event, levels = 0:2, labels = c("censored", "relapse", "death") ) lm_fac <- landmark_data(   subjects, patient_id, followup_days, event,   landmarks = c(30, 60, 90), horizon = 180 ) tidy(lm_fac, status_labels = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   landmark n_at_risk n_censored n_relapse n_death #>      <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>   <int> #> 1       30         8          3         3       2 #> 2       60         7          3         2       2 #> 3       90         5          1         3       1

what: tidylandmark: Tidy Workflows for Landmark Survival Analysis — tidylandmark-package
title: tidylandmark: Tidy Workflows for Landmark Survival Analysis — tidylandmark-package
text: Provides tidy framework landmark survival analysis, facilitating construction landmark-specific risk sets, incorporation longitudinal covariates, estimation associations time--event outcomes. Supports covariate estimation using last observation carried forward (LOCF) linear mixed-effects models (LME), alongside Cox proportional hazards Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Offers consistent reproducible workflow conducting analyses across multiple landmark times.
